note: FICTIONAL illustrative scenario for the RegChain prototype. The rule, the trial, the sites, the batches and the shipments are invented to show how RegChain handles a label that can no longer serve two countries. It is not a real Ministry of Health notice and not legal advice.

case.title: Israel: shared booklet labels no longer accepted
case.summary: From 3 January 2027, investigational products imported for Israeli sites must carry an Israel-only label in Hebrew with the Ministry of Health trial approval number. Multi-country booklet labels that also cover other countries are refused at import, even when they include Hebrew.
case.transition: Kits imported before 3 January 2027 under a shared booklet label may be used at the site until they expire.
case.consequence: The shared booklet for Israel, Greece and Cyprus can no longer serve Israel. Stock pooled across the three countries splits in two: the booklet batches stay with Greece and Cyprus, and Israeli sites need Israel-only kits.

evidence.excerpt: Investigational products imported for a clinical trial in Israel shall bear a label intended for Israel only.
A label shared with another country shall not be accepted at import from 3 January 2027.

items: Label language: Hebrew (required), English allowed alongside.
Shared booklet labels with other countries are accepted until 2 January 2027 (illustrative scenario: from 3 January 2027 an Israel-only label with the Ministry of Health trial approval number).
A Ministry of Health import approval for each shipment, quoted on the airway bill.
The batch's QP release documentation travels with the shipment.
